name: MDI HTTP Referer Block
author: Medium Interactive

sections.description:
MDI HTTP Referer Block lets site owners mark visitors that arrive from specified referrer domains and optionally:

  • Show a small notification (server-side) with the referrer host/path.
  • Hide specific elements (CSS selector).
  • Redirect flagged visitors to a different URL.
  • Use server-side referrer detection (PHP) and/or client-side detection (JS) for cases where referrer headers are missing.

Cookies used: mdi_syndicated_ref — the plugin sets this cookie for the configured number of days.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the mdi-http-referer folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Configure settings at: Settings → HTTP Referer.
sections.faq:
Will this expose the full referrer URL publicly?

No. The plugin only outputs host and path in the notification to avoid leaking query parameters. Referrer data is sanitized.

Does the plugin support regex matching?

The client-side code treats configured domain strings as patterns and will try to use them as regex. Keep patterns simple (example: example\.com or partner.example).

short_description: Hide elements or redirect users based on referrer domains. Useful for blocking partners, scrapers, or altering content per source.
